title: Difference laws carry only field-representable matroids
claim: (1) Every downset of subsets of a finite set containing the singletons is the free-set family of one relation (its support relation); so the Vamos matroid is carried by single relations, for example its support relation and a union of two GF(7) codes, and both relations' laws fail elimination. (2) Top lemma: a subdirect product of finite algebras in a Mal'tsev variety, each with a unique maximal congruence, is the full product exactly when its image in the product of the simple tops is full. (3) If every nontrivial subgroup of a finite group G has a unique maximal normal subgroup, every system of a law of cosets of subgroups of powers of G has as matroid a direct sum of one GF(p)-representable matroid per prime p and rank-one parallel classes; laws of affine subspaces over a finite field F carry F-representable matroids. (4) Hence the Vamos matroid, the non-Pappus matroid and the 2-sum of the Fano and non-Fano matroids never occur in such laws, nor in their shadows, lifts and disjoint unions. (5) In any law that composes like cycles, every pp-definable set has a unique maximal pp-definable equivalence, so tops exist. Open: whether every law that composes like cycles carries only direct sums of finite-field-representable matroids, and the top lemma for such laws.
failure_conditions: A support relation of a downset containing the singletons has a free family other than the downset, or a Vamos relation's free sets differ from the Vamos matroid or its circuit projection has no direct case whose two copies fail.
A subdirect product of groups with unique maximal normal subgroups is full while its top image is not, or the reverse.
A system over a group law as in (3) has free sets different from the direct sum of its per-prime GF(p) codes, or is not a matroid.
The Vamos matroid as defined is disconnected, binary or ternary.
Two proper pp-definable equivalences found in a law composing like cycles join to the total relation.
foundation_claim_scope: Which matroids the systems of a law can carry when its knots compose like cycles. No native recurrence, composed topology in the protected sense, path, metric distance or physical claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py verifies universality on 200 random downsets and both Vamos relations over all 256 subsets with failing circuit projections, the top lemma on 60 random subdirect products for each of S3, D5, AGL(1,5), Z4, Z9, the per-prime decomposition on 60 random systems per group, the Vamos matroid's connectivity and non-representability over GF(2) and GF(3), unique maximal equivalences among derived equivalences of the lift, a shadow and Z9, and agreement with the census; four controls rejected; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with randomized checks; classical tools (Fleischer's lemma, modularity of congruence lattices, Goursat, Scott's lemma) cited; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: candidate-local-delta: the top lemma generalizes the Frattini argument and may be folklore in universal algebra; the matroid consequence for group laws and Proposition 6 (tops exist without a difference operation) are new to the program; the literature on secret-sharing and partition representations concerns uniform representations and does not apply to single relations here.
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-21.
